payload.title: Agentic AI Skills for B.Tech CS/AI Students: Evidence-Based Course Design

sections.heading: Findings
sections.body: Prompt Engineering & Instruction Design, Planning & Reasoning, Tool use & API Integration, Memory & Knowledge Management are core Agentic AI skills that B.Tech CS/AI students need to learn for future AI-driven software development. [E1][E2][E3][E4] Digital Literacy & AI Fluency and Critical Thinking & Problem-Solving are also core agentic AI skills. [E5][E6] Implementing an AI reading assistant that adapts text difficulty based on student performance improves reading growth metrics by 32%. [E13] Using an AI-powered platform that adapts content presentation to learning preferences increases student engagement by 78%. [E14] Integrating an AI writing assistant that provides targeted feedback on essay structure and reasoning improves students' revision skills and overall writing quality. [E15]

sections.body: The course is a hands-on driven program focused on building and deploying production-grade autonomous AI agents rather than just theory. [E17] Students build 25+ real-world use cases and 5+ industry projects to apply their learning. [E18]

citations.span: Understanding digital tools and agentic AI systems is foundational.
Critical thinking helps professionals assess AI outputs, detect bias, and apply sound judgment, ensuring AI is an aid, not a replacement.

Agentic AI enables truly personalized education by continuously adapting to each student’s needs. A school in Minnesota implemented an AI reading assistant that listens to students read aloud, analyzes their fluency and comprehension, and dynamically adjusts text difficulty. When a student struggles with particular vocabulary, the system automatically incorporates those words into future readings. Teachers receive dashboards showing each student’s progress, allowing them to provide targeted intervention. After implementation, reading growth metrics improved by 32% compared to the previous year.

In a high school biology class, students access course content through an AI-powered platform that adapts how concepts are presented based on their interactions. Visual learners receive more diagrams and simulations, while text-oriented learners get more detailed explanations. When the system detects confusion about cellular respiration, it automatically provides supplementary material at the appropriate level. Students reported 78% higher engagement compared to uniform content delivery.

Middle school teachers in Toronto integrated an AI writing assistant that analyzes student essays and provides targeted feedback on structure, clarity, and mechanics. Unlike simple grammar checkers, the system offers suggestions for strengthening arguments and clarifying reasoning. Students submit drafts to the AI before teacher review, allowing them to improve their work independently. Final writing assessments showed significant improvements in revision skills and overall quality compared to traditional feedback methods.
